title: Spring Framework Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: @Bean marks a value that Spring creates. The context is a container that lets the program find that value. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Spring calls the @Bean method to create the String. getBean reads that managed value by its type. Close the context when the program is finished.

exercises.question: The method name becomes the bean name. This example asks for the bean called school. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The factory method name school becomes the bean name. The lookup asks for that name and String type. The requested name must match a registered bean.

exercises.question: A container can hold several beans of one type. A name selects the one you need. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Both beans have type String. The explicit name blue selects one unambiguously. A lookup by type alone is ambiguous when two beans match.

exercises.question: Spring can pass one bean into another bean method. This is dependency injection: the object receives what it needs. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Spring creates Score first and passes it to badge. The Badge method doubles its stored 4. Declare the needed dependency instead of creating a second hidden copy.

exercises.question: The normal Spring scope is singleton: one instance per bean definition in the container. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The default scope returns the same Object on both lookups. Reference equality is therefore true. Singleton means one per container bean definition, not one in every program everywhere.

exercises.question: Prototype scope makes a new bean each time the container is asked for it. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Prototype scope calls the factory for each lookup. The two returned objects have different identities. Spring does not manage full destruction of prototype instances for you.

exercises.question: @Lazy delays this bean until it is requested. The print inside its factory shows when creation happens. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The lazy factory has not run at the first print. Requesting its bean then prints Made now. Lazy creation delays work; it does not remove that work.

exercises.question: @Value can read a property with a fallback. No lesson.score property is set, so the fallback is 8. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The property placeholder uses 8 after the colon because no matching property is set. A fallback is used only when the property is missing.

exercises.question: initMethod names a method Spring calls after making the bean. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Spring calls prepare after construction. That method stores Ready before the program reads text. The named method must exist and be callable with no arguments.

exercises.question: destroyMethod names cleanup. Closing the context runs it for this singleton bean. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The try-with-resources block closes the context. Spring then calls the bean cleanup method once. Cleanup needs the context to close; an abrupt process stop may skip it.

exercises.question: @Primary marks the preferred bean when several beans match a type. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Both factories return Strings, but @Primary tells a type-only lookup to prefer blue. Only one matching bean should be the primary choice.

exercises.question: containsBean lets code check a registered name before trying to read it. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The message bean name was registered from its factory. containsBean therefore reports true. A name check does not validate every future operation on the bean.
